$$\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{a}+\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{b}+\frac{c}{a}+\frac{a}{c}$$

Expanding the product of the two given sums:

$$(a+b+c)\left(\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c\right) = 3 + \left(\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{a}+\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{b}+\frac{c}{a}+\frac{a}{c}\right)$$

The diagonal terms $a\cdot\frac1a$, $b\cdot\frac1b$, $c\cdot\frac1c$ contribute 3, and every other term is one of the six ratios in the target sum.

Substituting the given values:

$$\left(\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{a}+\cdots\right) = 26\cdot 28 - 3 = 728 - 3 = 725$$
